text:
carla: hitting a flakey repro in the sampleapp where SSE chunks reorder after a client reconnect + auth refresh. seems related to debounce logic in the auth refresh path. root: first POSTs stream ok, client disconnects, refresh happens, reconnect resumes but chunks from old connection reappear after new ones.
ben: oof, can you paste the raw stream lines?
carla: yep — here's a trimmed snippet from the proxy logs and client stdout:
carla: ```
> event: chunk
data: {"id":"c1","index":1,"text":"hello"}

> event: chunk
data: {"id":"c2","index":2,"text":"world"}

(client disconnect)
(reconnect with Authorization: Bearer <refreshed>)

> event: chunk
data: {"id":"c2","index":2,"text":"world"}

> event: chunk
data: {"id":"c3","index":3,"text":"!"}
```
carla: note c2 gets duplicated and appears before c3 sometimes. ordering flips in a couple of runs.
dave: is the proxy using connection pooling/keepalive? could the old TCP connection be hanging in the proxy and replaying buffered chunks after reconnect?
carla: proxy is nginx + our stream-proxy service (go). stream-proxy logs show: `resume_token=abc123 sent_resume=true` then later `emit_chunk id=c2 source=old_conn`. looks like the resume code is toggling sources.
alice: could be an auth debounce window: client disconnect triggers token refresh, but we debounce refresh notification to the upstream router and both old+new connections end up registered as active for a small window. That would let late-old-chunks be emitted after new ones.
ben: interesting. can you repro with a very short TTL on tokens or by forcing immediate refresh? also try toggling `enable_resume_debounce=false` in sampleapp config.
carla: repro steps I used in sampleapp: 1) start stream 2) wait for 2 chunks 3) kill client socket 4) immediately call refresh endpoint 5) reconnect. I can try your flag.
devex-bot: reminder: file a bug with a minimal repro and include `--trace` logs. tag with `devex/streaming` and assign to eng-runtime.
carla: created issue https://redwood/issue/INF-4123 with logs and a tiny node+go repro. added `--trace` output.
dave: thanks. quick hack to check: on resume, add monotonic seq check on server side and drop anything with seq <= last_sent_seq for that stream id. that will make it safe while we fix root cause.
alice: good mitigation. we should also audit auth refresh path: debounce -> broadcast -> connection lifecycle. Might be a race between broker removing old connection and resume broadcast.
ben: low-risk patch: add a short drain-delay after marking old conn closed before allowing resume from new conn. if combined with seq check we should see no duplicates.
carla: testing drain-delay + seq-check now. will update the issue with results in ~15m. thanks all :thumbsup:
ben: fwiw, seen similar ordering flips when clients abort mid-chunk; keep an eye on partial chunk fragmentation too.
carla: good call — I saw one case where a chunk was split across two TCP packets and reconnect caused the second half to reattach to new stream. adding checks for `complete` flag in chunk envelope too.
dave: nice. once you confirm, let's ship a small patch in the stream-proxy and a sampleapp config change. devex: we should add a KB note about this repro and config knobs.
alice: agreed, add a short blurb to DX samples explaining resume caveats and how to toggle `enable_resume_debounce` and `drain_delay_ms`.
carla: updated issue with final repro and suggested patch. marking as needs-review.
ben: will take a look after lunch.
carla: thanks — will ping if I hit any more weirdness.
